newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe says France to relaunch Thomson sale quickly.
newsitem.headline: Juppe says France to relaunch Thomson sale quickly.

text.p: France will launch consultations to allow the stalled privatisation of electronics and defence giant Thomson SA to resume as quickly as possible, Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Wednesday, according to his office.
The government said earlier it had suspended the sale of Thomson because an independent commission did not agree with plans to sell part of the group to Korea's Daewoo.

"The government will launch consultations as rapidly as possible allowing the privatisation to take place on a basis that will be defined very quickly," Juppe's office quoted him in a statement as saying.
"The aim of privatising Thomson addresses the necessity for France to have an electronics and defence industry of global standing," he said.
The government announced in October its preference for selling Thomson to private electronics group Lagardere rather than rival bidder Alcatel Alsthom to create a competitive French defence group.

Lagardere said it planned to sell consumer electronics division Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo, sparking an outcry from workers and the Socialist opposition. The government said on Wednesday the privatisation commission also had doubts about this part of the plan and the sell-off had had to be suspended.
